title: One parcel fee, many item charges
hook: A fixed parcel fee is different from a fee attached to each item.

knows: that a model can declare hypothetical quantities
doesNotKnow: Separate per-parcel overhead from per-item charges when aggregating shipments.

misconception: Combining parcels removes every charge, including per-item charges.
objective: Separate per-parcel overhead from per-item charges when aggregating shipments.

claims.text: A fictional parcel costs €3 plus €0.50 per item. Items can share one parcel or each use a parcel. Scaled model; fictional policy; shared parcel permitted; no other fees.
claims.source: Declared hypothetical inputs and limits in resource-specs.json. No actual product, price, tariff, shelf-life, treatment or physical appliance specification is asserted. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The stage's two results are computed by the printed expressions. At Items=4, A=€14 and B=€5. Geometry follows the declared dimension relationships. Other pictures use a fixed full scale across the slider range; continuous fills and arcs show relative amounts rather than literal object counts.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*",3.5,"x"]; B=["+",3,["*",0.5,"x"]]; x denotes Items. At x=4, A=14, B=5. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. Diagram scale: resourceGraphicScale in resource-model.ts takes the maximum modeled magnitude across both formulas and the declared slider range. For non-geometry figures, full-scale values are displayed; the scale stays fixed when the slider changes. Energy axis endpoints use resourceAxisEnd, including B=5×A hours in lh-watts-hours-trade; cylinder rx and ry both scale with radius in resourceCylinderDimensions. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: The per-item charge repeats either way, but the fixed parcel fee repeats only with separate parcels. Labeling a cost as fixed requires naming the thing it is fixed per.
claims.source: src/lib/lifehacks/resource-specs.json contains this lesson's numeric AST; src/lib/lifehacks/resource-model.ts evaluates it. A=["*",3.5,"x"]; B=["+",3,["*",0.5,"x"]]; x denotes Items. At x=4, A=14, B=5. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals. The principle follows from those expressions and stated scenario limits. FC LH-1 (session 2, received by message): verified; see company/reviews/lifehacks-200/fact-check-LH1-2026-10-14.md.

claims.text: A fictional parcel costs €3 plus €0.50 per item. Shipping ten items in ten separate parcels instead of one costs how much more? Correct: €27. The per-item charge is the same either way; only the €3 parcel fee repeats, nine extra times: €27.

At x=4, A=14, B=5. Values are fictional/ideal assumptions, not measurements. Display rounds to at most three decimals.
